TEXT.English:
Mother Lyn is a figure shrouded in the mists of time. None can say with certainty how old she truly is. Some whisper she walked the ancient forests of the fairies original world before Ceridwens great teleportation, while others believe she was among the first to set foot on Erebus. What is undeniable is her timeless presence, a living bridge between the past and the present. Her wisdom is not merely learned but remembered, a tapestry woven from centuries of experience. Mother Lyns expertise lies in the quiet, hidden power of mushrooms and the secrets they hold. She tends to vast, labyrinthine gardens deep within the forests of Falyn, where rare and enchanted fungi thrive under her care.
As the spiritual and moral compass of the Court of Falyn, Mother Lyn embodies the values of the old ways. She is a steadfast advocate for the traditions that once united the fairies, believing that their ancestors wisdom holds the key to surviving, and thriving, in Erebus. Her guidance is rooted in fairness, honor, and an unshakable commitment to the natural order. She is a lawful soul, her word as binding as any oath sworn under the moon, and her judgments are delivered with both compassion and resolve.

Mithiray Ni Falyn is a figure of both reverence and unease within the Court of Falyn. Born into the enigmatic House Fane, she carries the weight of its ancient traditions and its unyielding pursuit of power through the mysteries of life and death. Mithiray is a tireless champion for the ideals of House Fane, seeking to weave its philosophy into the fabric of Falyns governance. She argues that the Court must embrace the full spectrum of magic, including the forbidden, if it is to survive in the harsh world of Erebus. Her influence is subtle but persistent, a whisper in the ears of the powerful, a shadow in the halls of decision. She does not demand loyalty; she earns it, through favors, knowledge, and the promise of power.
Beyond her arcane pursuits, Mithiray is an avid hunter. She stalks the forests not for sport, but for the thrill of the chase and the lessons it teaches: patience, precision, and the understanding that all things, even the mighty, can be brought low. Her hunts are legendary, and it is said that she can track her prey through the densest undergrowth, guided by more than just sight and sound.

After the delegation of the Bannor left the tent, Maraky relaxed in her chair and smiled. "Bring me some tea." She snared at her adjutant, watching them leave the tent behind the Bannor soldiers. Maraky was happy. Her plan worked out perfectly. Like it always does.
With a satisfied grin, she looked at the little group of healers in the corner of the tent. Well, Healers was their official term, yet they were so much more. They were her healers, healers from House Pesna. As much as they know how to heal others, they know exactly how to harm them as well. Toxins are just medications in other dosages after all.
"Good work. As always. I think we are done here. Give them the antidotes to the poisons we used on them. They were good and lawful enemies, so I will let half their soldiers live." The healers bowed, knowing too well what she meant by that. They would prepare as many false antidotes as real ones and give them to the enemies without any form of information about that. Half of them will die, while those lucky enough to receive a real antidote will live. That was the way Maraky liked to toy with others.

Pleia is a scion of House Nairu, a house renowned for its unmatched skill in the hunt and its unwavering dedication to the art of the bow. Pleias skill with the bow is legendary. She is said to be able to place an arrow between the eyes of her enemies long before they even realize they are within striking distance. Her shots are not just accurate, they are inevitable.
Recognizing the need for a force that could project the Court of Falyns power beyond its borders, Pleia founded an elite cadre of archers. These warriors are not merely soldiers, but they are artists of death, each handpicked and trained by Pleia herself. They serve as the Courts eyes and arrows, striking swiftly and silently, often turning the tide of battles before they truly begin. Under her command, they have become a symbol of Falyns reach and precision, a force that can shape the outcome of conflicts from the shadows.
Pleia is as much a hunter of opportunity as she is of game. She understands that power is not just won on the battlefield but also in the halls of influence. Her political acumen is as sharp as her arrows, and she knows how to cultivate alliances, and how to eliminate obstacles. It is no secret that those who oppose her often find themselves the victims of unfortunate "accidents". A rival might vanish during a hunt, or a foe might be found after a battle, their body riddled with arrows.

"Stop struggling so much." Kissania weaved another arcane binding around the angles of the human prisoner. The fairy floated around him, studying his body and how her many flew through him. "Interesting. Hm. What if I increase the output a bit?" With a small gesture of her hand, the magic intensified and the human screamed into his gag.
"This is already his limit? Gosh, I really need more robust ones! I should ask the trackers to bring me more Doviello men again. They at least survived several days. These farmers here have near no resistance. But well." She floated in front of her prisoner, who had nearly passed out and resisted not as she removed his gag. Her hands gently wrapped around his neck, she guided him forward and their lips met. A warmth encased his body and his soul. Then came the pull. Senses were dulled and vanished, his feeling for his body was gone as his soul left his body and entered her.
Encased in a strange serene warmth, he became trapped inside her. Kissania licked her lips as she removed the bindings of the corpse. It fell onto the ground. With a clap into her hands, fairies floated in to bring it away to the Candy Shop. Kissania herself began taking notes and already thought of what she would do with the next one.

"Marikya! Play more with your food." These were the words of her teacher that Marikya heard again and again in her mind. She never truly understood why so many of her kind toyed for so long with the lesser beings. For her, they were just food, just another soul to consume, another prey to hunt down. The hunt was fun for her, yet after it was over, she never saw any reason to toy with them further. A quick strike to weaken them and then a quick kiss to suck out their souls. That was all that her prey could expect from her.
Yet, in her efficiency, she stood alone. Many seeked her out to learn from her. How to track down a prey. How to sneak onto them. How to quickly enter a village and leave before the guards even realized that she was there. Marikya always told them the same.
"I am not invisible. But if you are small like me, and cute like me, the lesser ones see no threat in you till you are close enough to strike. Just wear something casual, hide your true nature and put on a smile. Oh, how many of them called me adorable or asked me if I was lost. It is truly kind of them, and their kindness is so easy to exploit."

"Kill me!" The proud soldier shouted towards the evil fae that smiled down towards him from the top of a tree. He was bleeding from many wounds, yet none of them were fatal enough. Laila giggled melodically as she jumped down, slid under his risen sword and made another cut before she jumped out of reach for the soldier to strike back.
"Oh, I will. Worry not." Laila proclaimed with a playful grin. "But why should we end our dance too soon?" She jumped forward, grabbed his sword hand and came close enough with her face, so that their noses touched. "Would you destroy a nice toy? Nah. I will play with you till you are truly unable to lift this silly metal stick you call a sword. And then, yes, then you will truly become mine." Her whispers sent a cold shower down his back.
Laila stepped back and evaded another strike. "I will eat your soul, hihi. So you better fight me more seriously if you want to meet your god. As I will ensure you, your soul will never reach the afterlife, but will be mine forever." The soldier tried to strike her again and again she evaded and made another shallow cut. "Yes. Try harder!"

Every evening, Sister Aramai visited the Dollhouse and the slaves living there. She was a welcomed guest, as her music brought peace and serenity to them. Like every evening, Bernd sat down and listened to her musik and like every evening, he hoped he would be chosen this time. Aramai wandered through the ranks of the slaves after her play, the poor souls all trapped in their serene trance. Then she took one of them and guided them out of the Dollhouse. They never returned, yet the slaves were sure that it was a good thing to be taken by her.
Little did they know what truly was their fate. Aramai was a Misrak Fairy after all and had little sympathy for the lesser races. The slaves she took were brought to her home, where she would toy with them, cuddle them and eventually, begin to slurp out their souls to consume them and trap them for eternity in her own spiritual world.

After weeks of travel, Eirene and her small group of fairy sisters and cousins reached civilized lands. They were met at first with caution, but after the monks learned that they were refugees and searched for a place to live in peace, they welcomed them in. The Elohim had welcomed Eirene and with her, she brought knowledge and the will to integrate into the society that welcomed her.
At first, the fairies under her care lived in the outskirts of the abbeys. They learned the ways of the monks and slowly gained their trust. Years passed and the first humans began to form families with the fairies, slowly integrating them more and more till they were finally allowed into all parts of Elohim society.
Eirene herself joined the defenders of the sacred places, learned their ways and began to protect what is holy in this dangerous world.

The people of her small village did not know that the Eternal Court had dissolved, had not heard that the command chain broke down. The orks came in the night and like many of her fairy sisters, Iskaya thought that they would just need to hold out till the Wildfae would arrive. Yet, they never came and the village lost most of its inhabitants that night.
The survivors fled in small groups, hoping to escape the ork scouts. Iskaya quickly became the leader of her small group. She did so not because she was the oldest, or the most experienced fighter, but because she was the most stubborn one. She refused to give up, she pushed her people forward. Eventually, they met others who fled from the orks.
Iskaya and her group joined the humans, and together they fled to the plains to join the forming Chislev. It did not matter that Iskaya was no human, as she shared the hate and the wish for revenge against the orks.
